title: CrossLight: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Cross-City Traffic Signal Control

problem.claim: Traffic signal control policies need to alleviate congestion and transfer effectively across cities.

gap.claim: Existing research primarily develops online or offline policies for specific cities, while transfer to new cities is hindered by limited high-quality data and costly, risky exploration.

contributions.claim: CrossLight combines meta-training on offline source-city data with adaptive fine-tuning in a target city.

The approach reconstructs trajectory dynamics, dynamically builds city topological structures, distills pattern-structure-aware trajectory representations, and uses MAML to identify initial parameters.
Target-city adaptation uses a rank-and-filter replay buffer and an exploration strategy to balance exploitation and exploration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CrossLight as an innovative cross-city traffic signal control paradigm and describe its methodology as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four cities, the authors report comparable performance in new cities with minimal fine-tuning iterations.
The authors report that CrossLight surpasses existing online and offline methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reinforcement learning is presented as a promising approach to traffic signal control and congestion reduction.
City-specific online and offline policies face transfer barriers caused by data limitations and costly exploration.

CrossLight performs offline source-city meta-training and target-city adaptive fine-tuning using reconstructed dynamics, topology-aware representations, MAML initialization, and replay-buffer filtering.
Experiments across four cities are reported to show comparable new-city performance with few fine-tuning iterations and superiority over online and offline baselines.
The authors characterize the framework as a feasible and effective solution for intelligent transportation.

source_observation.claim: Combining offline source-domain learning with limited online target-domain adaptation is reported to support cross-city policy transfer.

interpretation.claim: A staged offline-to-online strategy may reduce the amount of risky exploration required when adapting a policy to a new environment.

application.claim: For other cross-domain control problems, pretrain transferable representations from source data and reserve online interaction for targeted fine-tuning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the strategy transfers under substantially different domains, data quality, or exploration constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, traffic environments, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail the baseline implementations, fine-tuning iteration counts, or replay-buffer and exploration parameters.
